Thanks for the call earlier, Marissa — this was really helpful.

Quick recap on our side to make sure we're aligned on POC goals/success criteria: 
- Evaluation target: integrate Redwood API into our customer-facing summarization flow and compare latency/cost vs our current on-prem solution.
- Success criteria: 99th percentile latency < 250ms for short prompts, end-to-end response quality within 5% of baseline on our eval set, and overall token cost below $0.002/token for production-like throughput.
- Traffic pattern: steady test load ~30 qps during daytime tests, but we may need bursts up to ~120 qps during simulated load windows.
- Timeline: start POC the week of Mar 8, 2-3 week evaluation.

Two questions we have for planning:
1) For the POC can you recommend reserved capacity and burst strategy so we can avoid throttling during our high-load tests?
2) Who will own the infra plan and the onboarding for the Redwood side (technical point of contact)?

Also, can you send the capacity plan spreadsheet you mentioned? That will help our infra team size things on their end.

Thanks,
Alice

Alice — great notes, thanks for summarizing. Copying Rishi (SE) and Vivek (CS) to propose a concrete capacity and ownership plan.

Proposed POC approach (high level):
- Reserved capacity: start with 2 reserved GPU instances (A100-class equivalent) to provide predictable baseline throughput.
- Burst capacity: allow burst to up to 8 GPUs via autoscaling during simulated load windows; bursting will be subject to available pool capacity in the region.
- Autoscaling policy: target CPU/GPU utilization thresholds and queue depth-based scaling to open/close burst nodes automatically; warm cache pre-warming before large tests.
- KV/prefix caching: we'll configure prefix caching for your steady-state requests to reduce token cost for repeated prompts.

Rishi — could you share a quick spreadsheet with the initial sizing (tokens/sec estimates, expected concurrent sessions) and any operational caveats (warm-up, cold-starts, estimated token cost at given concurrency)?

Next steps:
- Rishi to send capacity_plan_v1.xlsx by EOD today.
- Vivek to schedule an onboarding call for Mar 9 (preferred) or Mar 10.
- Marissa will send proposed POC statement of work and success criteria doc.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 14:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC discovery call — capacity plan (attachment)

Hi Alice — attaching the capacity_plan_v1.xlsx and a short architecture note (redwood-poc-architecture.pdf). Summary below so you have the key numbers up front.

Short summary (POC sizing):
- Baseline: 2x A100-class GPUs reserved. Expected steady throughput ~30 qps with median latency ~80-120ms and p99 ~220-260ms depending on prompt length.
- Burst plan: autoscale up to +6 GPUs (total 8) for up to 30 minutes during simulated stress windows. We recommend scheduling large-scale burst tests (load windows) rather than uncontrolled open burst.
- Warm-up: recommend 10-15 minute warm-up period before peak tests to populate KV cache and reduce p99.
- Autoscaling policy: scale-out when request queue depth > 25 for 30s or GPU util > 70% for more than 60s. Scale-in with conservative cooldown (5-10 minutes) to avoid thrash.
- Expected token cost: estimated $0.0016–$0.0022/token at the recommended batch sizes and quantization settings — final depends on exact prompt distribution.

Operational notes:
- If you need guaranteed burst capacity beyond our regional pool, we can pre-approve burst reservations (subject to contract) — otherwise burst is best-effort and may be constrained during region-wide peaks.
- For privacy/regulatory requirements we can run this POC in a VPC-private deployment if required, but that adds setup time (~2-3 days).

Attachments: capacity_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with detailed qps/token math), redwood-poc-architecture.pdf (diagram + recommended config).

Let me know if you'd like a quick walkthrough on Friday.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
